# WAS_Merging_Extended { #wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended }

```python
WAS_Merging_Extended(
    df,
    da,
    dem=None,
    date_month_day='08-01',
    varname=None,
    projection='utm',
    utm_zone=None,
    hemisphere=None,
    kriging_cv=True,
    kriging_fixed=None,
    kriging_cache=True,
    kriging_cache_key='global',
    max_grid_points_warn=200000,
    verbose=True,
)
```

Merging class for station observations with gridded estimates,
using geostatistical and machine learning methods.

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [adjust_duplicates](#wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.adjust_duplicates) | If any values in the Series repeat, nudge them by a tiny increment |
| [plot_merging_comparison](#wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.plot_merging_comparison) | Create a side-by-side scatter plot comparing observations against |
| [transform_cdt](#wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.transform_cdt) | Convert a CDT‑format station data frame to an xarray Dataset. |
| [transform_cpt](#wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.transform_cpt) | Convert a CPT‑format station data frame to an xarray Dataset. |
| [validate_merging_methods](#wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.validate_merging_methods) | Leave-one-year-out validation of all merging methods at station points. |

### adjust_duplicates { #wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.adjust_duplicates }

```python
WAS_Merging_Extended.adjust_duplicates(series, increment=1e-05)
```

If any values in the Series repeat, nudge them by a tiny increment
so that all are unique (to avoid indexing collisions).

### plot_merging_comparison { #wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.plot_merging_comparison }

```python
WAS_Merging_Extended.plot_merging_comparison(
    da_corrected,
    da_estimated=None,
    missing_value=-999.0,
)
```

Create a side-by-side scatter plot comparing observations against
the original estimation and a corrected field.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type         | Description                                                               | Default    |
|---------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| da_corrected  | xr.DataArray | Corrected field (output from a merging method) with dimensions (T, Y, X). | _required_ |
| da_estimated  | xr.DataArray | Original estimation grid. If None, uses self.da.                          | `None`     |
| missing_value | float        | Missing value indicator for observations (passed to transform_cpt).       | `-999.0`   |

### transform_cdt { #wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.transform_cdt }

```python
WAS_Merging_Extended.transform_cdt(df, missing_value=-999.0)
```

Convert a CDT‑format station data frame to an xarray Dataset.
Expects first three rows: station names, longitudes, latitudes, elevations.

### transform_cpt { #wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.transform_cpt }

```python
WAS_Merging_Extended.transform_cpt(df, missing_value=-999.0)
```

Convert a CPT‑format station data frame to an xarray Dataset.
Expects first two rows: station names, then latitudes, then longitudes.
(The second row is used for LAT, the third for LON – but here we assume
 the input has exactly two metadata rows: first row station names,
 second row LAT, third row LON. The class will handle it as in the first version.)

### validate_merging_methods { #wass2s.WAS_Merging_Extended.validate_merging_methods }

```python
WAS_Merging_Extended.validate_merging_methods(
    missing_value=-999.0,
    min_points_year=5,
    k_nearest=10,
)
```

Leave-one-year-out validation of all merging methods at station points.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type   | Description                                                         | Default   |
|-----------------|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| missing_value   | float  | Missing value indicator for observations (passed to transform_cpt). | `-999.0`  |
| min_points_year | int    | Minimum number of test points required to include a year.           | `5`       |
| k_nearest       | int    | Number of nearest stations to use for RF/XGB feature engineering.   | `10`      |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                             |
|--------|--------------|-----------------------------------------|
|        | pd.DataFrame | Mean RMSE per method, sorted ascending. |
